title: Refresh token still mints tokens after RFC 7009 revocation
vulnerable_behaviour: POST /revoke returns 200 (as RFC 7009 requires) but does not mark the refresh token revoked; the refresh_token grant continues to mint new access tokens.
fixed_behaviour: POST /revoke marks the refresh token revoked; this laboratory additionally revokes access tokens issued from the same grant under its supported-token policy.
termination_trigger: explicit token revocation: POST IdP /revoke token_type_hint=refresh_token (200)
declared_expected_scope: access tokens issued from the same grant
protected_operation: POST IdP /token with the revoked refresh token, followed by successful GET RS /api/data as the expected subject using the minted access token
cwe_rule_path: termination trigger present (RFC 7009 revocation acknowledged with 200)
artifact presented after the trigger (refresh token)
protected operation succeeded (new token minted and usable at the expected resource)
=> explicit-termination failure: revocation acknowledged but not enforced

neighbour_rules.CWE-613 original sense (time-only expira: not matched: refresh tokens here have no expiry; the failure is on the explicit path

uncertainty.reason: revocation response and the subsequent successful grant are both in the trace; no third party involved

lifecycle_event: explicit token revocation: POST IdP /revoke token_type_hint=refresh_token (200)
normative_basis: Explicit token-revocation contract for the revoked refresh token in the laboratory.
